transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-10-06
- Time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~62m
- Attendees: Avery Cole (Redwood AE), Devika Rao (Redwood SE), Markus Liang (Head of ML at Sable), Priya Nair (Infra Lead), Jonas Becker (CTO), Lina Ortiz (PM)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be imperfect):
Redwood walked through a cost playbook for a 3-week POC focused on Sable's chat summarization product. Main constraints: monthly budget cap for POC (equiv to $8k), p95 latency target for 256-token responses <= 250ms, and end-to-end throughput for peak of 50 r/s. Action items to exchange traffic sample and run synthetic benches.

Transcript body:
[00:00:02] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round of intros — we'll keep it tight, the goal is to land on a POC plan for economics and benchmarking.
[00:00:15] Markus: Hi, Markus here. we run the summarization backend for our knowledge product, roughly 15M tokens/day now in staging but production would be more, uh, looking to validate costs and latency before commit.
[00:00:27] Priya: Priya, infra. we manage GCP and some on-prem gpu racks, curious about private options and data residency.
[00:00:32] Devika: Great, thanks. quick note, I'm the SE, I'll own bench harness and metric collection with you.
[00:00:38] Jonas: Jonas, CTO, i'm mostly interested in the runway math — how many tokens can we serve under our budget and what knobs to pull.
[00:00:45] Avery: Perfect. First, let's capture success criteria. Markus, what would success look like for the POC?
[00:00:55] Markus: Two things: 1) demonstrate p95 generation latency below ~250ms for our 256-token median case, and 2) show a per-1M-token cost that maps to our target — we're aiming for <$40 per 1000k tokens? excuse me, that's messy. goal is $8k budget for 3 weeks so we need a sense of cost per token.
[00:01:18] Lina: Also product wants quality parity — regression no more than 5% on ROUGE-or whatever metric we use vs current model.
[00:01:25] Devika: okay, so three buckets: latency SLO, cost cap, quality guardrails. We'll scope bench types that target each.

[00:01:40] Avery: Let's talk baseline per-token estimate. Redwood typical hosted generator baseline for a 7B-ish dense model under standard FP16 on an A100 equiv is around 0.00045 USD per token for long-form? Devika, can you add color?
[00:01:55] Devika: Yeah, rough ballpark depends on sequence length and batch size. For 256 tokens with a sequence-length of ~512 effective (prompt+gen), if we run with batching at 8 and no KV cache between requests, you'll see higher per-token. If we enable prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts and batch to 16 on peak loads, token cost drops materially — maybe 20–40% savings. But real numbers need the exact model and quantization.
[00:02:22] Priya: what's the delta between hosted and dedicated? we have spare nvidia T4s and some A5000s on prem.
[00:02:29] Devika: Dedicated can bring down unit compute cost — less operator margin — and predictable throughput. Hosted gives fastest onboarding and we can recommend smaller model variants or quantized ones. For on-prem you'd need Redwood Private, which supports customer KMS and private control plane but we need to scope network egress and storage.
[00:02:46] Markus: Cost sensitivity — if caching removes 30% of tokens and batching adds another 20%, that compounds right?
[00:02:52] Devika: Exactly. If you cache prefixes and avoid recomputing system prompt, plus hit rate on cache is 40–60% for your workload, that reduces token compute significantly. But caching and batching are workload-dependent: short tail / unique prompts don't batch well.

[00:03:12] Jonas: For benchmarking, what do you need from us?
[00:03:16] Devika: We'll ask for: a 48-hour sampled live traffic dump (anonymized), a canonical set of 10k prompts representing typical sessions, and an SLO matrix — targets for throughput, latency percentiles, and quality thresholds. Then we'll synth run: synthetic concurrency + recorded-replay.
[00:03:32] Markus: We can export request logs; are you okay with pseudonymized IDs?
[00:03:36] Avery: Yes, anonymized is fine. We'll also share a benchmark harness — a dockerized runner that can play back requests at configured qps and measure p95, p99, cpu/gpu util, memory, and token counts.

[00:03:52] Priya: security/compliance — we need SOC2 and encryption at rest; if data leaves our VPC for hosted, what controls exist?
[00:03:58] Avery: Redwood hosted is SOC2 Type II, we support TLS in transit, encryption at rest, and customer key management options for Private. For POC we can do hosted with a limited dataset under NDA. For stricter needs, Private VPC option is possible but adds ~2-3 weeks to provision.
[00:04:18] Devika: Also audit logs and per-token usage dashboards we'll provide; useful for mapping cost back to product features.

[00:04:30] Lina: timeline question — can we complete this in 3 weeks?
[00:04:34] Avery: Yes, typical econ POC: week 1 gather artifacts and pipeline setup; week 2 run controlled benches and iterate on batching/caching; week 3 run final runs, analyze unit economics and produce a recommend plan.
[00:04:45] Devika: We'll do an early quick-run in week 1 to catch obvious config issues — that's helpful.

[00:05:00] Jonas: Walk me through an example calculation — say we want to estimate monthly spend if product goes GA at 100 r/s, average 200 generated tokens per request.
[00:05:12] Devika: Quick math: 100 r/s * 200 tokens = 20k tokens/s = 1.728B tokens/day. Multiply by per-token compute cost. If hosted baseline is $0.00045 token (again depends), that's ~777k USD/day — obviously unrealistic, you'd need optimizations. So instead you answer with model selection, quantization, batching, and caching to drive per-token down to cents per thousand tokens (c/1k). For example targeting $2–6 per 1k tokens vs $450 per 1k in naive compute.
[00:05:44] Markus: That naive number scares me — we need clarity on the units: per-token vs per-1k tokens.
[00:05:49] Devika: Right — we should frame as per-1k tokens. Our spreadsheet has columns: model variant, seq len, avg tokens, batch size, estimated tokens/sec per GPU, effective cost per 1k tokens under that config. We'll share.

[00:06:10] Avery: Let's be explicit about knobs we'll test: 1) model family (7B vs 13B quantized), 2) batch size (1,4,8,16), 3) KV/prefix cache hit rates (0, 25, 50, 75%), 4) response length caps (truncate to 128 vs 256), and 5) lower-precision quantization (int8 vs fp16).
[00:06:28] Devika: For each run we'll capture: tokens generated, GPU utilization, latency p50/p95/p99, and cost-per-1k. We'll also compute amortized throughput per GPU to recommend fleet needs.

[00:06:45] Priya: about caching — if our product uses session-based context and a lot of repeated system prompt, can you do prefix caching with cross-request KV reuse? We're concerned about stale cache and memory blowup.
[00:06:56] Devika: We support granular cache eviction policies and size caps. For session-based reuse, a 30–60 minute TTL is common. If memory grows, you can shard cache across GPUs or use sticky routing. We will propose a configuration for POC.

[00:07:10] Markus: Any quick wins we should try on day 1 to reduce costs?
[00:07:14] Devika: Yes: shorten max_generation, use top-k/top-p tuning to reduce token churn if quality remains OK, enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, and try int8 quantization on a smaller model variant for comparable quality.

[00:07:30] Jonas: On the metrics side, how will we attribute cost back to features?
[00:07:34] Avery: We'll instrument per-route token breakdowns in the console, and tag requests by feature flags. That way you can see cost per feature and make product tradeoffs (e.g., summarize long docs only on premium plan).

[00:07:48] Lina: About SLOs — is 250ms p95 feasible with a quantized 7B on a single GPU?
[00:07:54] Devika: For 256 tokens, hitting 250ms p95 on a single GPU is tight but achievable with optimized kernels, short prompt lengths, and small batch sizes (1–4). If you need concurrency, use more GPUs or a lower-latency tier. We'll measure both latency-first and cost-first configs.

[00:08:10] Markus: I'd like a scenario table: best quality, balanced, and cheapest, with expected $ per 1k tokens and p95 numbers.
[00:08:16] Avery: Agreed — that's what our econ-playbook spreadsheet generates. We'll produce three recommended configs and the expected unit economics.

[00:08:30] Priya: Does Redwood provide a tool to estimate monthly spend for a given qps and token profile?
[00:08:35] Devika: Yes — the cost-playbook sheet accepts qps, avg prompt tokens, avg response tokens, cache hit rate, and batching assumptions to produce estimated monthly spend and GPU counts. We'll send that link.

[00:08:48] Markus: For security approval, who do we need to loop in from Redwood?
[00:08:51] Avery: I'll introduce you to our Security Solutions Architect, and we can share the SOC2 report and our data flow diagram. For Private, we will engage infra to plan VPC peering.

[00:09:05] Jonas: Ok, let's lock down timeline and owners. If we start the artifact exchange tomorrow, realistic target for initial bench run?
[00:09:12] Devika: If we get the 48h sample and prompt set by Monday, we can stand up the harness and do a smoke run by Wednesday. Full runs and iteration take through next week.

[00:09:22] Avery: So action items and dates: we'll send the sheet by Friday; customer to send logs by Monday; Devika to provide bench runner by Tuesday; first smoke bench Wednesday; larger runs Thursday/Friday. Final report following week.

[00:09:36] Markus: Sounds good. small nit: can you include a column for egress and storage costs? those matter for our org.
[00:09:42] Avery: Yes, we'll add egress and storage line items.

[00:09:50] Lina: For vendor comparison — we may run parallel quick test vs Anthropic/OpenAI just to benchmark latency. any thoughts?
[00:09:56] Devika: It's fine to run parallel tests; Redwood can help run head-to-head on the same prompt set so you see true delta in latency and cost. For hosted closed models you may need separate accounts.

[00:10:08] Jonas: Any gotchas we should watch for during benching?
[00:10:11] Devika: Warmup and KV priming are important. Also, throttling and retries on load tests can distort p95. We'll provide a playbook to avoid common pitfalls and recommended run durations to reduce variance.

[00:10:25] Priya: On the POC environment — will we need network peering for Private?
[00:10:28] Avery: Yes for Private you'll do VPC peering; for hosted POC you can use a secure tunnel or our transient API keys with IP allowlist. We'll detail both options.

[00:10:40] Markus: One last question — can Redwood estimate cost sensitivity to 10% change in cache hit rate?
[00:10:45] Devika: Yes, the spreadsheet includes sensitivity columns; we'll show delta tables: cost per 1k at cache rates 0/25/50/75%.

[00:10:55] Avery: Great. quick recap and then we'll close.
[00:10:58] Avery: Recap: Success criteria (p95 <=250ms, 3-week $8k budget constraint, quality regression <=5%), artifacts needed, bench harness and spreadsheet, timeline with smoke run mid-week, and security intro.
[00:11:12] Markus: Thanks — excited to see numbers.
[00:11:14] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[00:11:16] Devika: we'll follow up with links and the runner.

[00:11:20] End of meeting notes (auto-trim). Some low-confidence transcribed fragments may contain misheard technical terms.
